title: Book One · Chapter 30: Ask Again
story:
The class display begins after the last lesson. Before then, the children have reading, sums, and one short making time.

Ronan keeps looking at the brown kite by the wall. From his chair, he can see Mr Qiu's new line. He can also see that one side of the tail hangs lower.

During making time, Leo wants to colour the paper red.

"We have brown," Ronan says.

"A red kite makes people look up."

"Ours is brown. People keep looking down at it. We know that."

Leo laughs. Then he puts the red pencil away. There is more useful work to do.

Miss Wu comes over. She has a list of names and a little paint mark on her wrist. Three children want her at once.

"What's your question?" she asks.

"How do we make it fly?" Ronan says.

"I can't answer all of that in one minute. Show me one problem."

Ronan points to the tail. The yellow square is tied much nearer one side. He lifts the kite. That corner hangs low.

"Should this be in the middle?"

Miss Wu holds the top while he looks. "What does your drawing show?"

The drawing has its tail straight below the long stick. Their real tail is tied round the wrong crossing point near one edge.

Leo touches the knot. "The paper was strong here. I put the knot here."

"That kept the tail on the kite," Miss Wu says. "Now look at the two sides. Are they level?"

She must go to the paint table. The boys don't get a whole lesson. They can work on the tail now.

Ronan puts the kite flat. Leo loosens the tail knot. They move it to the bottom of the long stick and test it above the desk. The shape hangs straighter.

Then Leo points to the new flying line. "We moved two things."

"The tail and Mr Qiu's line."

"Both things changed before a test. Maybe one helped. Maybe both helped. We cannot tell."

They draw both changes on their page. They changed the line this morning. Now they changed the tail, too. They write both changes down. For the next try, only the meeting knot will move.

Mei passes their desk with her garden picture. She stops to look at the test page.

"Those arrows are all down."

"So far," Ronan says.

Mei takes a spare blue pencil and puts it beside the page. "For later. Don't use my good dark one."

"Do you want your picture beside our kite?" Ronan asks. She shakes her head. Her garden will go beside the paper houses. She chose that place with Miss Wu.

After lunch, the boys make a small card with both their names. Under the names, with help spelling, they write: OUR KITE. STILL LEARNING TO FLY.

Leo doesn't like the last line at first. He says it sounds like a baby bird.

"But it does not fly yet," Ronan says. "Our card needs to say that."

Leo reads it again. Then he adds a little bird with a very flat head at the bottom.

They carry the card to Miss Wu. She checks the words then asks, "Where will you stand?" They choose one side each. Both boys will have room to speak. They can stand side by side.

The first parents arrive. Ronan's stomach feels tight. The card is clear. The kite is whole. He knows people may ask about flying. He will tell them the kite has not flown yet. The card says that, too. He and Leo can show them the card.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：points＝指向；tail＝尾巴；middle＝中间；changes＝改动。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 问了哪个更具体的问题？
2. 他和 Leo 决定一次只改变多少事情？
